title: San Marco
name: San Marco
metaTitle: San Marco 1031 Exchange Services in Jacksonville, FL
metaDescription: San Marco 1031 exchange coordination for boutique retail and medical office replacement property near San Marco Square and the hospital campus.

sections.html:
San Marco sits across the St. Johns River from downtown by way of the Main Street Bridge, and its replacement-property scope centers on two distinct demand drivers: the boutique retail and restaurant buildings fronting San Marco Square, and the medical office development that has grown up around the nearby hospital campus.

A submittal package for San Marco should specify which of these two demand drivers a target property serves, since the underwriting approach, lease structure, and tenant-credit review differ meaningfully between the Square's retail base and the hospital-adjacent medical office category.

sections.heading: Boutique Retail and Medical Office Scope Around San Marco Square
sections.html:
San Marco Square carries a walkable cluster of small-format retail, restaurant, and service tenants in low-rise historic buildings, a format that trades on foot traffic and neighborhood draw rather than highway visibility. Medical office development along Hendricks Avenue and the streets nearer the hospital campus has grown as a separate but adjacent category, generally in newer construction than the Square's historic core.

Residential density immediately surrounding the Square has remained high relative to other historic Jacksonville neighborhoods, and that density supports the Square's restaurant and boutique-retail tenant base independent of any single anchor draw.

sections.heading: Property Types
sections.html:
San Marco's qualifying inventory generally sorts into the following categories:

  • historic mixed-use buildings fronting San Marco Square
  • single-tenant medical office near the hospital campus
  • boutique restaurant buildings with outdoor seating areas
  • small office buildings in converted residential structures
  • single-tenant retail along Hendricks and Atlantic Boulevard

A buyer weighing the Square's retail formats against the hospital-adjacent medical office category should compare lease-term stability and tenant-improvement recapture separately, since the two categories are priced on different bases in this submarket.

sections.heading: Square-Fronting Building Specifications
sections.html:
Buildings fronting the Square are generally small-footprint and low-rise, and a specification review should confirm current signage allowances and any historic-district review requirements before a renovation or tenant buildout is priced into the underwriting. Outdoor seating areas common to the Square's restaurant tenants should be reviewed for permit status separately from the base lease, since that use is not always automatically transferable to a new operator.

Second-floor space above the Square's ground-floor retail is frequently configured as office or residential, and a rent roll should list that upper-floor income separately from the ground-floor retail lease, since the two categories carry different renewal patterns.

sections.heading: Medical Office Diligence Near the Hospital Campus
sections.html:
Medical office tenants near the hospital campus should be reviewed for hospital-system affiliation the same way as in the Southside submarket, since that distinction affects both lease renewal probability and how a lender treats the income stream. Newer medical office construction in this corridor generally carries longer initial lease terms than the Square's retail and restaurant stock, which changes the hold-period math for a buyer comparing the two categories side by side.

Parking ratios at newer medical office buildings in this corridor are generally more generous than at the Square's older retail stock, and a buyer should confirm that ratio against the specific specialty practices in the tenant mix, since some specialties draw higher patient-visit volume per square foot than others.

sections.heading: Sequencing With Riverside as Paired Submarket
sections.html:
Riverside, across the river and connected by the same downtown-adjacent employment base, shares enough of San Marco's mixed-use and boutique-retail demand logic to function as a natural backup identification. A qualified intermediary should be engaged before a preferred Square-fronting property goes under contract, since this small, well-known node does not carry deep inventory and qualifying listings move quickly once priced correctly.

Lender coordination should be arranged early as well, since financing for a boutique-format Square building can take longer to underwrite than a standard net-lease acquisition given the smaller comparable-sales pool available for this specific format.

faqs.q: What distinguishes San Marco Square retail from a standard net-lease acquisition?
faqs.a: The Square trades on foot traffic and neighborhood draw in a walkable, low-rise historic format, rather than highway visibility, so underwriting should weight pedestrian counts and event programming at the Square more heavily than traffic counts, since a traffic-only model will understate the location's actual draw.

faqs.q: Does outdoor seating at a San Marco restaurant transfer automatically to a buyer?
faqs.a: Not necessarily. Outdoor seating permits for restaurant tenants should be reviewed separately from the base lease, since that use is not always automatically transferable to a new operator or a new tenant, and reapplying for the permit can take longer than a typical exchange timeline allows if it is discovered late.

faqs.q: How should a buyer evaluate medical office tenants near the hospital campus?
faqs.a: By confirming whether each tenant is hospital-system affiliated or an independent practice, since that distinction affects lease renewal probability and how a lender treats the income stream, and by comparing lease term length against the Square's shorter retail terms.

faqs.q: What backup submarket pairs naturally with San Marco?
faqs.a: Riverside, on the opposite bank and tied to the same downtown-adjacent employment base, shares enough of San Marco's mixed-use demand logic to serve as a practical backup identification, though its historic-district review requirements should be confirmed separately since they are not identical to San Marco's.

faqs.q: Why does timing matter for San Marco Square acquisitions specifically?
faqs.a: The Square is a small, well-known node without deep inventory, and qualifying listings tend to move quickly once priced correctly, so intermediary and lender coordination should begin before a preferred property is located rather than after a buyer has already identified a specific building.
